scope: Selected decisions for external stream data and caller-owned resolution.

decisions.premise: The viewer's image decoders run in a confined worker without filesystem or network access; the worker boundary remains intentional.
decisions.review: Retain. The ordinary PDF reader refuses external stream data before decode rather than opening a document-derived path or allowing the worker to fetch. No defect follows from not implementing a file/network broker.

decisions.premise: Read file specifications as values, but never follow arbitrary paths in the viewer reader.
decisions.review: Retain. It supports a separation between naming a file and accessing its contents. Table 5 /F is a stream source pointer, and the reader has no path resolution seam.

decisions.premise: External bytes are resolved by a caller and passed into pure archive conversion via ArchivePlan::external_data; the CLI's explicit local resolver is constrained to a file beside the source and does not fetch URLs.
decisions.review: Retain and distinguish from viewer reading. This is an implemented conversion route, so a narrow integration test can verify that nondefault FDecodeParms moves with caller-supplied bytes and remains effective after embedding. Existing test uses only Predictor 1 and checks dictionary text, motivating the scratch draft.

decisions.premise: FFilter/FDecodeParms without F do not identify external stream data and are inert for reading the embedded stream; conversion can strip them while retaining bytes.
decisions.review: Retained as the adopted interpretation. Existing archive test covers stripping orphan FFilter. No new reader behavior failure is claimed.

decisions.premise: The optional conversion CLI resolves only the constrained path form, never a URL or arbitrary path traversal.
decisions.review: Retain; this is an owner/tool access policy and does not narrow the PDF source text about how a supplied external stream is filtered.
